chapter.heading: Hormah
chapter.v:
The Canaanite
king of Arad who lived in the Negev learned that the Israelites were approaching on the road to Atharim. He went and attacked Israel and took some of them prisoners.

So Israel
made a solemn promise to the Lord: “If you hand these people over to us, we pledge to completely destroy their towns.”

The Lord
responded to their appeal and handed over the Canaanites to them. The Israelites completely destroyed them and their towns, and named the place Hormah.
chapter.heading: The Snake of Fiery Copper
chapter.v:
The Israelites
left Mount Hor by the road leading to the Red Sea so they could avoid traveling through the country of Edom. But the people became bad-tempered on the way

and made
complaints against God and against Moses, saying, “Why did you lead us out of Egypt to die in the desert? We don't have bread or water, and we hate this awful food!”

So the
Lord sent poisonous snakes to attack them, and many Israelites were bitten and died.

The people
went to see Moses and told him, “We were wrong to make complaints against the Lord and against you. Please pray to the Lord to get rid of the snakes from us.” Moses prayed to the Lord on their behalf.

The Lord
told Moses, “Make a model of a snake and put it on a pole. When anyone who has been bitten looks at it, they will live.”

Moses made
a snake out of bronze and put it on a pole. Those who looked at it did live.
chapter.heading: Camping on the Way to Moab
chapter.v:
The Israelites
left and camped at Oboth.

Then they
moved on from Oboth and camped at Iye-abarim in the desert on the east side of Moab.

They left
there and camped in the Valley of Zered.

Then they
moved on from there and camped on the far side of the Arnon River, in the desert near Amorite territory. The Arnon River is the border between the Moab and the Amorites.

That's why
the Book of the Wars of the Lord refers to “the town of Waheb in Suphah and the canyon of the Arnon,

the canyon
slopes that reach the village of Ar that lies on the border with Moab.”

From there
they moved on to Beer, the well where the Lord told Moses, “Have the people gather together so I can give them water.”

Then the
Israelites sang this song: “Pour out water, well! Everyone of you sing to it!

The tribal
chiefs dug the well; yes the leaders of the people dug the well with their rods of authority and their walking sticks.”The Israelites left the desert and carried on to Mattanah.

From Mattanah
they traveled to Nahaliel, from Nahaliel to Bamoth,

and from
Bamoth to the valley in the territory of Moab where the top of Mount Pisgah looks down on the wastelands.

Then Israel
sent messengers to Sihon, king of the Amorites, with the following request:

“Please allow
us to travel through your country. We won't cross any of your fields or vineyards, or drink water from any of your wells. We will stay on the King's Highway until we have passed through your country.”

But Sihon
refused to allow the Israelites to travel through his territory. Instead, he called out his whole army and went out to meet the Israelites head-on in the desert. When he arrived at Jahaz, he attacked the Israelites.

The Israelites
defeated them, killing them with their swords. They took over his land from the Arnon River to the Jabbok River —but only as far as the border of the Ammonites, because it was well defended.

The Israelites
conquered all the Amorite towns and took them over, including Heshbon and its surrounding villages.

Heshbon was
the capital of Sihon, king of the Amorites, who had fought against the previous king of Moab and had taken from him all his land as far as the Arnon River.

That's why
the old songwriters wrote: “Come to Heshbon and have it be rebuilt; restore the town of Sihon!

For a
fire blazed out from Heshbon, a flame from the town of Sihon. It burned up Ar in Moab where the rulers live on the high places of Arnon.

What a
disaster you face, Moab! You are all going to die, people of Chemosh! You handed over your sons as exiles and your daughters as prisoners to Sihon, king of the Amorites.

But now
we have defeated the Amorites! Heshbon's rule has been destroyed all the way to Dibon. We wiped them out all the way to Nophah and on to Medeba.”

The Israelites
occupied the country of the Amorites.

Moses sent
men to explore Jazer. The Israelites conquered its surrounding villages and expelled the Amorites living there.

Then they
continued on the road towards Bashan. Og, king of Bashan, led his whole army out to meet them head on, and fought them at Edrei.

The Lord
told Moses, “You don't need to be afraid of him, because I have handed him over to you, along with all his people and his land. Do to him what you did to Sihon, king of the Amorites, who ruled from Heshbon.”

So they
killed Og, his sons, and all his army. Nobody survived, and the Israelites took over his country.
